Main Economic Indicators
Sources and Definitions
The OECD publishes a range of short-term economic indicators which provide an at-a-glance picture of the
most recent changes in the 29 OECD economies and in ten non-member countries with which the OECD
has an ongoing programme of co-operation. Indicators are also published for the Euro zone. The indicators
published in MEI each month include: quarterly national accounts, business surveys, retail sales, industrial
production, construction, consumer prices, total employment, unemployment and balance of payments.
This publication supplements the monthly Main Economic Indicators.It provides explanations on the
sources and definitions used by individual Member countries and selected non-member countries to
compile the short-term indicators currently presented in the MEI. The current publication also describes a
number of data presentational aspects such as index linking and the compilation of zone aggregates.
This publication complements another forthcoming OECD publication which compares key aspects of
statistical methodologies used by OECD and selected non-member countries in the compilation of some of
the short-term economic indicators published in MEI.
ALSO AVAILABLE ON CD-ROM
The MEI database is also available on CD-ROM, in user-friendly software, Beyond 20/20TMfor WindowsTM,
that allows the users to extract data, prepare graphs and tables and perform their own analysis. It covers
a longer time period, with many series starting as early as 1960.

ORGANISATION FOR ECONOMIC CO-OPERATION
AND DEVELOPMENT
Pursuant to Article 1 of the Convention signed in Paris on 14th December 1960, and which came into
force on 30th September 1961, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
shall promote policies designed:
– to achieve the highest sustainable economic growth and employment and a rising standard of
living in Member countries, while maintaining financial stability, and thus to contribute to the
development of the world economy;
– to contribute to sound economic expansion in Member as well as non-member countries in the
process of economic development; and
– to contribute to the expansion of world trade on a multilateral, non-discriminatory basis in
accordance with international obligations.
The original Member countries of the OECD are Austria, Belgium, Canada, Denmark, France,
Germany, Greece, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain,
Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, the United Kingdom and the United States. The following countries
became Members subsequently through accession at the dates indicated hereafter: Japan
(28thApril1964), Finland (28th January 1969), Australia (7th June 1971), New Zealand (29th May 1973),
Mexico (18th May 1994), the Czech Republic (21st December 1995), Hungary (7th May 1996), Poland
(22ndNovember 1996) and Korea (12th December 1996). The Commission of the European Communities
takes part in the work of the OECD (Article 13 of the OECD Convention).

FOREWORD
This publication outlines methodologies used to compile short-term economic indicators published
by the OECD for Member countries, and for non-member countries within the programme of activities
of the Centre for Co-operation with Non-Members (CCNM). The indicators they describe are those
published in the June 2000 edition of the OECD monthly publication, Main Economic Indicators
(MEI).
The primary purpose of this publication and the forthcoming companion publication, Main
Economic Indicators: Comparative Methodological Analysis, is to provide users with methodological
information applicable to data produced by individual countries. Such information is essential to
ensure appropriate use by analysts of the indicators published. The information will also enable
national statistical institutes, and other agencies responsible for compiling short-term economic
indicators to compare their methodologies and data sources with those used in other countries. Finally,
it will provide a range of options for countries in the process of creating their own indicators, or
overhauling existing indicators.
Earlier editions of Main Economic Indicators: Sources and Definitions have been published by the
OECD, the last dating back to July 1997. The on going updating of MEI methodological information,
which was suspended in late 1998 to facilitate the development of a new database system, has now
recommenced. A revised text that reflects the prevailing content will be made available in the MEI
CD-ROM, other electronic products, and on the Internet.
The companion publication, Main Economic Indicators: Comparative Methodological Analysis
will, for the first time, provide an extensive analysis of the methodologies countries use to compile
short-term economic indicators published in MEI. This analysis will focus on issues of data
comparability in the context of existing international guidelines and recommendations published by
the OECD and other international agencies such as the United Nations Statistical Division, the
International Monetary Fund and the International Labour Organisation.
The OECD Secretariat gratefully acknowledges the contribution of the national statistical institutes
and the various national authorities responsible for short-term economic indicators, and thanks them
for their co-operation. Without this assistance it would not have been possible to produce this
publication.
Acknowledgement is also gratefully made to the United Nations Statistical Division, the
International Labour Organisation, the International Monetary Fund and the Statistical Office of the
European Communities for country methodological information which has been used to supplement
and clarify the methodological information provided by national agencies.

FOREIGN TRADE
Definition: Foreign trade data refer to general trade.
Exports are valued f.o.b. and imports are valued on
cost, insurance and freight (c.i.f.). Goods in transit
and almost all re-exports are excluded. Repairs on
goods, and oil procured in ports by carriers are
excluded.
Coverage: Trade with North Korea and Cuba is
excluded.
Collection: Foreign trade statistics record physical
movements of goods across the frontier. Data are
compiled daily from official custom declarations
collected by the 53 custom houses of the country,
where imports and exports transactions are notified.
Calculation: For conversion to US dollars (by
source), the weekly market average rate is used.
Annual and quarterly data are averages of monthly
figures.
Source: Korea Customs Administration
BALANCE OF PAYMENTS
Definition: Balance of payments data are compiled
in accordance with the 5th edition of the Balance of
Payments Manual published by the IMF (BPM5),
and presented according to the Standard
Presentation. Methodological details (in Korean)
are available in the annual publication of the Bank
of Korea: "About the Balance of Payments of
Korea".
Coverage: Data cover all the geographic territory
administered by the government of Korea.

CZECH REPUBLIC
Collection: Data are based on customs declarations
obtained via Single Administrative Documents
(SADs). SADs are processed as they are collected,
leading to ongoing revisions. Since 1992, the
Combined Nomenclature has been used.
Calculation: Annual and quarterly data are
averages of monthly figures. Data presented in
dollars are obtained by converting the monthly
figures expressed in national currency using the
monthly average exchange rate. Prior to 1993, data
are expressed in CSFR koruny. From 1993, foreign
trade data take account of amendments to customs
legislation which were introduced on 15 January
1996.
Source: Czech Statistical Office
BALANCE OF PAYMENTS
Definition: In principle, data are compiled
according to the 5th edition of the Balance of
Payments Manual published by the IMF (BPM5),
and presented according to the Standard
Presentation. Some items (e.g. insurance services,
interest and financial derivatives) are not fully in
compliance with BPM5 procedures due to lack of
information.
Coverage: The balance of payments vis-à-vis the
Slovak Republic is included.
Calculation: Consolidated Balance of Payments
comprise convertible currencies and
non-convertible currencies.
Financial account balance, $ mln
Definition: Data refer to capital and financial
accounts. Data exclude changes in official reserves.
Source: Czech National Bank

FOREIGN TRADE
Definition: Trade system used is special trade
principal and are based on the regulations issued by
the Council or Commission of European Union;
Exports are valued f.o.b. and imports are valued
c.i.f.
Collection: The data on trade in goods between
Finland and other Community member states are
obtained from Intrastat statistical declarations. The
basic data on the trade between Finland and
non-member countries are obtained from Customs
declarations.
Calculation: Annual and quarterly data are
averages of monthly figures. Data presented in US
dollars are obtained by converting the monthly
figures expressed in national currency using the
monthly average exchange rate.

BALANCE OF PAYMENTS
Definition: Balance of payments data are compiled
in accordance with the 5th edition of the Balance of
Payments Manual published by the IMF (BPM5),
and presented according to the Standard
Presentation.
Coverage: Capital account includes unrequited
transfers such as debt forgiveness and grants from
European Union funds.
Collection: The source data for the goods balance
are National Board of Customs data on foreign
trade. Compilation of travel balance statistics is
based partly on households surveys. Other current
account items and investment compilations are
based on company surveys.
Calculation: Annual data are sum of quarterly data.

POLAND
Collection: Data are derived from customs
declarations made on the Single Administrative
Document (SAD) and from January 1998 data are
derived also from the reduced administrative
document. From 2000, the coverage of enterprises
has been extended to include units in the entire
national economy. Prior to that date, only
enterprises in the mining, quarrying manufacturing
sectors were covered.
Calculation: Annual and quarterly data are
averages of monthly figures. Data presented in
dollars are obtained by converting the monthly
figures expressed in national currency using the
monthly average exchange rate.
Source: Central Statistical office of Poland (GUS)
BALANCE OF PAYMENTS
Definition: Balance of payments data are compiled
in accordance with the 5th edition of the Balance of
Payments Manual published by the IMF (BPM5),
and are presented according to the Analytical
Presentation. Methodological details are available
in the monthly publication of the Polish National
Bank: "Information Bulletin".
Collection: The data are compiled on the basis of
settlements recorded by the Polish banking system
between Polish residents and the rest of the world.
Calculation: Data are compiled on a cash basis in
millions of US dollars. Annual and quarterly data
are the sum of the monthly figures.
Net income, $ mln
Definition: Net income comprises net interest.
Unclassified transactions, $ mln
Definition: Data refer to the net amount of
purchase and sale of foreign currencies which are
used mainly for foreign transactions.
Financial account balance, $ mln
Definition: Data refer to capital and financial
accounts. It comprises exceptional financing and
excludes changes in official reserves.
Change in official reserves, $ mln
Definition: Change in official reserves comprise
adjustment for changes in the prices in official
reserves and other assets and liabilities. From 1997,
excluding valuation changes. Components such as
cash, current accounts and deposits (assets and
liabilities) have been transferred to the Financial
and Capital account.
Source: Bank of Poland

SPAIN
Net foreign position, Ptas bln
Definition: Data refer to the net global position of
private banks with the rest of the world.
Calculation: Data refer to end of period.
Source: Bank of Spain
FOREIGN TRADE
Definition: Data refer to special trade. Exports are
valued f.o.b. and imports are valued on cost,
insurance and freight (c.i.f.).
Coverage: The statistical frontier coincides with the
geographical boundary.
Collection: The Customs Authority is responsible
for collecting Foreign Trade statistics. Data are
recorded at the moment when merchandise is
delivered to the customs. For extra-European Union
countries data are collected from the administrative
documents [Single Administrative Document,
(SAD)], and INTRASTAT declarations for trade
within the European Union.
Calculation: Annual and quarterly data are
averages of monthly figures. Data presented in US
dollars are obtained by converting the monthly
figures expressed in national currency using the
monthly average exchange rate.
Source: Customs Authorities, Spain
BALANCE OF PAYMENTS
Definition: Definition: Balance of payments data
are compiled in accordance with the 5th edition of
the Balance of Payments Manual published by the
IMF (BPM5), and presented according to the
Standard Presentation. Methodological details are
available in the annual publication of the Bank of
Spain: "Balanza de pagos de Espanya".
Coverage: Data cover the territory of Spain.
Collection: The sources of information are customs
declarations and INTRASTAT data for
merchandise trade, and data collected directly by
the Bank of Spain from commercial banks and
corporate companies.
Calculation: Data are compiled monthly, on an
accrual basis.
Financial account balance, Ptas bln
Definition: Data refer to capital and financial
accounts.
Change in official reserves, Ptas bln
Calculation: A positive sign indicates a decrease in
assets and a negative sign an increase according to
the IMF sign conventions.
Source: Bank of Spain

Net services, SKr bln

Net income, SKr bln
Definition: Data refer to compensation of

other investments.

Net current transfers, SKr bln
Definition: Data comprise both current and capital
transfers.
Current account balance, SKr bln
Definition: The current account balance comprises
net transactions in goods and services and net
income from investments and transfers.
Financial account balance, SKr bln
Definition: From 1992 it refers to capital and
financial accounts. Change in official reserves are
included from 1992.

TURKEY
BALANCE OF PAYMENTS
Definition: Balance of payments data are compiled
in accordance with the 5th edition of the Balance of
Payments Manual published by the IMF (BPM5).
Coverage: Data refer to the economic transactions
of residents of Turkey with the rest of the world
during a month. Data covers Turkey.
Collection: Data are obtained from a variety of
sources including foreign exchange records of the
Central Bank and commercial banks, the State
Institute of Statistics, the survey on tourism receipts
and expenditures and the survey on shuttle trade.
Calculation: Transactions are valued at market
prices. Annual data are the sum of quarterly data.
Trade balance, $ mln
Definition: Exports f.o.b. and imports f.o.b. are
compiled on a special trade basis.
Collection: The State Institute of Statistics derives
the data from customs declarations. Data on
non-monetary gold are taken from banks’ foreign
exchange records.
Calculation: Original imports are valued c.i.f. and
are adjusted to remove the cost of insurance and
freight. Amounts deducted for insurance and freight
services to non-residents are re-entered in Net
services.
Source: Central Bank of Turkey
Net services, $ mln
Definition: This series covers net services
(transportation, travel and other services) and net
income. Income includes compensation of
employees as well as investment income.
Collection: Data are derived from banks’ foreign
exchange and other records, and sample surveys
conducted by the Central Bank. Reinvested
earnings on direct investment are taken from
Treasury records.
Calculation: Net services include income from
services and interest.
Source: Central Bank of Turkey
Financial account balance, $ mln
Definition: Data refer to capital and financial
accounts. Data exclude changes in official reserves.
Source: International Monetary Fund (IMF)

Collection: Euro zone Balance of Payments data
are compiled by the ECB (all monthly and the
quarterly/annual financial and income accounts)
and Eurostat (quarterly/annual current and capital
accounts) with the assistance of the national central
banks (NCBs) participating in the European System
of Central Banks (ESCB). For details of the
compilation methods used by national agencies
please refer to the individual countries.
Calculation: Balance of Payments data are
published at three frequencies: monthly (key items
only), quarterly and annual. The scope, underlying
concepts and breakdown are different for the
monthly and the quarterly/annual data (for example,
while data are in theory compiled on a transactions
basis, for the monthly data national income data can
be recorded on a cash basis). The ECB compiles the
figures for the euro area by aggregating the
participating countries' transactions vis-à-vis non-
residents of the euro area for all items except the
portfolio investment account and the financial
derivatives account. Compilation methods for the
last two items are different due to difficulties in
identifying the holders of securities issued by
domestic residents: moreover financial derivatives
are compiled as net transactions only. Pre-1999 data
are expressed in ecu’s converted at the prevailing
exchange rate. From 1999 they are expressed in
euros. Data presented in US dollars are obtained by
converting the monthly figures expressed in
national currency using the monthly average
exchange rate.
Change in official reserves, Euros bln
Definition: Reserve assets of the euro area consist
of the Eurosystem's reserve assets, i.e. under the
effective control of the ECB or the NCBs of
participating countries. They refer to highly liquid,
marketable and creditworthy foreign (non-euro
area) currency-denominated claims on
non-residents of the euro area, plus gold, SDRs and
the reserve positions in the IMF of the participating
NCBs.

Source: National Bank of Slovakia
Definition: Trade statistics include re-exports and
re-imports but exclude exports and imports of
services. From 1991 imports and exports are both
valued f.o.b. Imports also include transit charges for
goods delivered by pipelines and goods used by
other countries to pay back their debt to the Slovak
Republic.
Coverage: From 1993, imports and exports include
trade with the Czech Republic.
Collection: Since the beginning of 1991 foreign
trade statistics have been based on customs
declarations and the Harmonised System used. The
Unitary Customs Declaration was introduced in the
Slovak Republic on 1 January 1992. The returns are
processed by the Central Customs Administration,
established separately in the Slovak Republic in
early 1993.
Calculation: Since 1 January 1991 exports of goods
have been recorded at the time that confirmation of
their departure has been received. Imports of goods
are recorded at the date of their release from
bonded warehouses rather than at the date they
cross the frontier. Revisions to the data are made
retrospectively as returns are processed.
Source: Statistical Office of the Slovak Republic
